annotations.description: Activated Expedition Map to search for a land (goes to hand, can't play until next turn) instead of casting Planar Atlas, which costs the same 2 mana but stays on the battlefield as a permanent mana source AND filters the top 4 cards for a land. With only Urza's Tower as a land and needing to develop mana, the permanent ramp from Planar Atlas is more valuable than just tutoring a land to hand.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Expedition Map ({2}, tap, sacrifice) to search for a land card to put in hand.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Planar Atlas for {2} to get a permanent mana source and filter top 4 for a land, preserving Expedition Map for later when there's spare mana.

annotations.description: Playing Awakener Druid with only one Forest on the battlefield risks losing the only green mana source if either the Druid or the animated Forest is removed. The opponent has blue mana and 5 cards in hand, potentially including removal like Waterknot.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Awakener Druid, animating the only Forest into a 4/5 creature
annotations.betterLine: Cast Planar Atlas to develop mana, search for Urza's Mine (working toward Tron), and preserve the Forest as a safe mana source. Could then cast bigger threats next turn with more mana available.

annotations.description: Used Waterknot when Sailor of Means would develop the board and create a Treasure token to accelerate toward Courser of Kruphix (turn 5) and Rampaging Baloths (turn 6). The opponent's threats are all tapped/sick this turn, so there's no immediate need for removal. Master's Rebuke in hand could also deal with the 4/5 Treefolk later if needed.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Waterknot (presumably targeting the 4/5 Forest Treefolk or Awakener Druid) using all available mana
annotations.betterLine: Play Island, cast Sailor of Means (1/4 blocker + Treasure token), accelerating toward Courser of Kruphix next turn and Rampaging Baloths soon after. Save Waterknot or Master's Rebuke for later if the Treefolk becomes problematic.

annotations.description: Playing Urza's Factory (enters tapped) instead of Forest costs 1 mana this turn. Forest would enter untapped, providing 4 mana total and enabling casting Thaumaturge's Familiar (3) + Universal Solvent (1) in the same turn. Forest also provides green mana needed for future spells. Urza's Factory doesn't complete Tron (missing Power-Plant) and its 7-mana activation is very expensive.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Urza's Factory (enters tapped), leaving only 3 mana available this turn
annotations.betterLine: Play Forest (enters untapped) for 4 mana this turn, enabling more efficient sequencing like Thaumaturge's Familiar + Universal Solvent. Save Urza's Factory for a turn where the tempo loss of a tapped land matters less.

annotations.description: Passed priority in postcombat main with 2 untapped mana and Universal Solvent (costs {1}) available to cast. Universal Solvent is a pure-upside deployment — getting it on the battlefield early gives future access to its {7},{T},sacrifice removal ability at no cost. Walking Ballista as X=1 (1/1) was also castable with the remaining mana.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, ending the turn with 2 mana unused and castable spells in hand.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Universal Solvent for {1} to deploy it for future use. Could also consider Walking Ballista for X=1 with the remaining mana, or save 1 mana. At minimum, Universal Solvent should have been played.

annotations.description: Cast Walking Ballista as a 2/2 (X=2, 4 mana) instead of Golem Artisan (3/3 for 5 mana). With Tron completing next turn (Urza's Power Plant in hand), Golem Artisan's repeatable pump and keyword-granting abilities would be extremely powerful with 10+ mana available. Golem Artisan is both a bigger body now and has far more upside with the massive mana coming online.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Walking Ballista for X=2 as a 2/2, leaving 1 mana unused
annotations.betterLine: Cast Golem Artisan (3/3 for 5 mana) to maximize board presence and set up its powerful activated abilities with Tron mana coming next turn

annotations.description: Activated Walking Ballista to ping for 1 damage (likely to face or a 4-toughness creature that won't die), shrinking the 4/4 Ballista to 3/3, instead of deploying Universal Solvent which has significant future utility as a permanent destruction threat, especially with Urza Tron lands available.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Walking Ballista to remove a +1/+1 counter and deal 1 damage
annotations.betterLine: Cast Universal Solvent for {1} to deploy a threat that can later destroy any permanent for {7}, preserving Walking Ballista's 4/4 body for combat

annotations.description: Removed a +1/+1 counter from Walking Ballista (reducing it from 4/4 to 3/3) just to deal 1 damage to the opponent's face at 20 life. The 1 point of face damage is nearly meaningless while the counter has significant value keeping Ballista larger for combat. The Ballista is sick and can't attack this turn anyway, but the counter should be preserved for future use - either to kill an actual threat, finish off a damaged creature, or maintain board presence as a larger body.
annotations.actionTaken: Pinged opponent's face for 1 damage with Walking Ballista, reducing it from 4/4 to 3/3.
annotations.betterLine: Hold the counter on Walking Ballista to maintain it as a 4/4 for future combat or save the ping for a more impactful target later.

annotations.description: Shrinking Walking Ballista from 4/4 to 3/3 to deal 1 damage to opponent's face is poor value. The opponent is at 20 life, so 1 ping is negligible, while the Ballista loses significant combat presence. No opponent creature dies to just 1 damage, so there's no efficient removal available either. The Ballista should be preserved at full size to attack next turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Walking Ballista to ping opponent's face for 1, reducing it from 4/4 to 3/3.
annotations.betterLine: Don't activate Walking Ballista at all. Keep it at 4/4 to maximize its combat threat next turn when summoning sickness wears off. Save counter removal for when it can finish off a creature or deal lethal damage.

annotations.description: Removed the last +1/+1 counter from Walking Ballista to deal 1 damage to the opponent at 20 life, killing the Ballista. With Urza's Tron assembled, the Ballista could have been grown with its {4} activated ability in future turns, making it a significant threat. All three pings going to face at 20 life is low-value; the first two pings were already committed but saving the last counter would have kept the Ballista alive.
annotations.actionTaken: Removed the third and final +1/+1 counter from Walking Ballista to deal 1 damage to opponent's face (total 3 damage to a 20-life opponent), killing the Ballista.
annotations.betterLine: Decline to activate the third time, keeping Walking Ballista as a 1/1. With Tron online generating 7+ mana, Ballista could be grown with its {4} ability to add counters, becoming a much larger threat over time. A 1/1 body also blocks, carries equipment, and provides future flexibility.

annotations.description: Walking Ballista had 2 +1/+1 counters and Tron was assembled (Urza's Mine + Power Plant + Tower), generating 7+ mana. Instead of keeping Ballista alive and using the {4} ability to grow it into a serious threat, the player is removing all counters to deal just 2 damage to an opponent at 20 life, killing the Ballista for negligible impact.
annotations.actionTaken: Removed +1/+1 counters from Walking Ballista to deal 2 damage to opponent at 20 life, killing the Ballista
annotations.betterLine: Keep Walking Ballista alive with its counters. With Tron assembled, use {4} to add +1/+1 counters each turn, growing it into a major threat. A 2/2 that can grow with excess mana is far more valuable than 2 damage to a 20-life opponent.

annotations.description: Haiku Perfect activated Urza's Factory during combat to create a 2/2 token, which uses up all the Tron mana (7 generic + tap Factory). This prevents casting Ulvenwald Hydra in the postcombat main phase. With the Forest in hand played post-combat, they would have had exactly enough mana (2 Forests for GG + Tron lands for 4 colorless) to cast the 6-mana Ulvenwald Hydra, which would enter as approximately a 7/7 with reach, and tutor a land (potentially becoming 8/8). A 7/7+ reach that tutors a land is vastly superior to a 2/2 token.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Urza's Factory during combat to create a 2/2 Assembly-Worker token, tapping all Tron lands.
annotations.betterLine: Pass during combat, then in postcombat main phase play Forest from hand, then cast Ulvenwald Hydra (4GG) using both Forests and Tron lands. Hydra enters as ~7/7 reach and tutors another land to the battlefield.

annotations.description: Spent 8 mana (7 + tap Factory) during combat to create a 2/2 Assembly-Worker token, when the mana could have been used postcombat to cast Golem Artisan (5 mana, 3/3 with pump abilities for artifact creatures) which is strictly better. The 2/2 token can't even attack this turn since it was just created during combat.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Urza's Factory to create a 2/2 token during combat, using essentially all available mana
annotations.betterLine: Tap Factory for {C} instead, then in postcombat main phase cast Golem Artisan (3/3 with relevant pump abilities) and potentially also play the Forest from hand and cast Thaumaturge's Familiar

annotations.description: Blocked the 1/3 flying Thaumaturge's Familiar instead of the 2/2 Assembly-Worker Token. Blocking the token would prevent 1 more damage (taking 1 instead of 2) and kill a creature that deals more damage. Additionally, Rampaging Baloths doesn't have reach or flying, so blocking a flyer should be illegal - but even if the game allowed it, blocking the 2/2 is strictly better since it prevents more damage.
annotations.actionTaken: Blocked Thaumaturge's Familiar (1/3 flying) with Rampaging Baloths
annotations.betterLine: Block the Assembly-Worker Token (2/2) with Rampaging Baloths to prevent 1 more damage and kill the higher-power attacker

annotations.description: At 4 life in a critical position, Haiku Perfect activated Urza's Factory before playing Urza's Mine from hand. Playing the land first would have made Ulvenwald Hydra 9/9 instead of 8/8 (its P/T equals lands controlled), and provided additional mana for Golem Artisan activations to pump creatures or grant evasion. The land drop is free and strictly improves the board before committing mana to Factory.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Urza's Factory before playing the Urza's Mine land from hand.
annotations.betterLine: Play Urza's Mine first to grow Ulvenwald Hydra to 9/9, then activate Urza's Factory with the additional mana available, leaving more mana open for Golem Artisan activations to grant trample/flying or pump creatures.

annotations.description: At 4 life facing Rampaging Baloths 6/6 (which generates 4/4 tokens on landfall) plus an existing 4/4 Beast token, creating a 2/2 Assembly-Worker is far less impactful than using Universal Solvent to destroy Rampaging Baloths. The Baloths is the most dangerous threat both as a 6/6 trampler and as a token generator. A 2/2 token barely helps with blocking when the opponent has 6/6 trample.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Urza's Factory to create a 2/2 Assembly-Worker token for 7 mana.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Universal Solvent ({7}, {T}, sacrifice) to destroy Rampaging Baloths, eliminating both the 6/6 trample threat and the ongoing landfall token generation that would quickly overwhelm the board at 4 life.

annotations.description: Opponent is at 4 life. Next turn, G31FL Stats can attack with Rampaging Baloths 6/6 (trample) and Beast Token 4/4. However, opponent has Ulvenwald Hydra 8/8 and Golem Artisan 3/3 that can both block next turn, potentially stopping all damage. By not casting Master's Rebuke to kill Golem Artisan (using Baloths' 6 power to deal 6 to the 3/3), the opponent gets an extra blocker that could prevent lethal.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting Master's Rebuke
annotations.betterLine: Cast Master's Rebuke targeting Rampaging Baloths (or any creature with 3+ power) and Golem Artisan 3/3 to remove a key blocker, ensuring lethal attack next turn with Baloths + Beast Token against only Ulvenwald Hydra as a blocker.

annotations.description: Targeted the Assembly-Worker Token (which is sick and not attacking) with Golem Artisan's +1/+1 ability during combat, wasting the buff entirely. The token can't attack this turn, so the +1/+1 does nothing.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted Assembly-Worker Token (sick, not attacking) with Golem Artisan's +1/+1 ability
annotations.betterLine: Target Ulvenwald Hydra or Golem Artisan (both attacking) with the +1/+1 to deal 1 extra damage, bringing opponent from 19 to 5 instead of 6. Every point matters when you're at 4 life facing Rampaging Baloths.

annotations.description: Gave trample to a summoning-sick Assembly-Worker Token that isn't attacking and can't attack this turn. The token is 2/2 with no combat relevance this turn without haste. Meanwhile, the opponent has no untapped blockers (Courser, Baloths, and Sailor are all tapped), so giving it haste would have allowed it to attack for 2 additional unblocked damage. At 4 life facing lethal next turn from Rampaging Baloths + Beast Token, every point of damage matters.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose trample for the Assembly-Worker Token
annotations.betterLine: Choose haste to allow the summoning-sick Assembly-Worker Token to attack for 2 additional unblocked damage (15 total instead of 13)

annotations.description: At 4 life facing lethal on the crackback, Haiku Perfect should maximize damage. Giving Assembly-Worker Token haste (2 mana) adds a 2/2 attacker, then using remaining 2 mana for a +1/+1 pump yields 16 total damage (1+9+4+2). Starting with +1/+1 pump first may lead to suboptimal mana allocation and potentially 1 less damage.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose +1/+1 pump on Golem Artisan first
annotations.betterLine: Give Assembly-Worker Token haste first to add it as an attacker, then use remaining mana for +1/+1 pumps to maximize total combat damage (16 vs potentially 15)

annotations.description: At 4 life in a desperate race against Rampaging Baloths and a Beast token, Haiku Perfect declined to activate Golem Artisan a second time with 2 available mana. This cost 1 point of damage (opponent goes to 5 instead of 4). With 0 cards in hand, there's no reason to hold mana back.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority instead of activating Golem Artisan's +1/+1 ability a second time
annotations.betterLine: Activate Golem Artisan again targeting itself for another +1/+1, making it 5/5 and dealing 15 total damage instead of 14, putting opponent to 4 instead of 5

annotations.description: With Urza's Tower untapped (producing 3 colorless due to Tron), the player could afford another Golem Artisan activation for {2} to pump an attacking artifact creature +1/+1. No blockers are available, so all combat damage goes through. Missing 1 point of damage (16 vs 15 total) leaves the opponent at 4 instead of 3, which matters when Haiku Perfect is at only 4 life themselves.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without using remaining mana for a second Golem Artisan pump activation.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Golem Artisan again targeting any attacking artifact creature for +1/+1, dealing 1 additional point of combat damage to bring the opponent closer to lethal range.

annotations.description: With opponent attacking for 15 total damage (2+9+4), declining to cast Master's Rebuke to kill Golem Artisan (4/4) means taking 15 instead of 11 damage, going to 4 life instead of 8. At 4 life, G31FL Stats is extremely vulnerable to counterattack, while at 8 life there's much more breathing room. The Beast Token 4/4 can deal exactly 4 damage to kill Golem Artisan.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting Master's Rebuke during opponent's combat
annotations.betterLine: Cast Master's Rebuke targeting Beast Token 4/4 to deal 4 damage to Golem Artisan 4/4, killing it and reducing incoming damage by 4 (surviving at 8 life instead of 4)

annotations.description: G31FL Stats passed on casting Master's Rebuke during opponent's combat, taking 15 damage (going from 19 to 4 life) instead of killing either Thaumaturge's Familiar or Golem Artisan to save 4 damage and remove a threat. The Beast Token 4/4 (summoning sick but still a valid source for Master's Rebuke) could deal 4 damage to kill either the 2/4 Familiar or the 4/4 Golem Artisan. With the opponent at 4 life, preserving life total is critical.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting Master's Rebuke during opponent's attack
annotations.betterLine: Cast Master's Rebuke targeting Beast Token 4/4 to deal 4 damage to Thaumaturge's Familiar (killing the evasive flyer) or Golem Artisan (killing the pump engine), reducing incoming damage from 15 to 11 and removing a significant threat
